To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SFRP-2 is secreted by mammary tumor and normal cells, is incorporated into the ECM, interacts with fibronectin and integrin, and promotes cell adhesion, inhibits apoptosis and induces tumorous transformation.
SFRP2 promotes cell adhesion and inhibits apoptosis by interacting with fibronectin, and this antiapoptotic activity is dependent on the fibronectrin-integrin connection.
the SFRP2 protein is secreted and interacts with ECM proteins, and this interaction is required to induce tumorous phenotype and inhibit cell apoptosis.

the role of Sfrp2 in mammary tumor progression and its interaction with the extracellular matrix, which may provide novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying the tumorigenesis of canine mammary tumors.
the role of secreted Frizzed-related protein 2 in mammary carcinogenesis.
the biological role of secreted frizzled-related protein (SFRP) 2, a novel member of the SFRP family, in the mammary gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SFRP-2 is a tumor-associated protein and that the antiapoptotic activity of this protein is mediated through fibronectin and integrin.
SFRP-2 is a novel regulator of apoptosis and cell adhesion and that it may play a role in mammary tumourigenesis.
SFRP 2 is involved in mammary tumor progression and that its action is mediated via ECM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SFRP2 protein is secreted and can bind to fibronectin in the ECM of tumor cells, which may be the mechanism by which SFRP2 promotes cell adhesion and protects cells from apoptosis.
SFRP-2 is an important regulator for mammary tumorigenic processes and its action is closely related to its interaction with ECM.
SFRP 2 is secreted from the cells and is incorporated into the ECM, and it can interact with fibronectin and the integrin protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SFRP proteins are secreted and incorporated in the extracellular matrix.
SFRP proteins are not just Wnt inhibitors.
